content.thinking: I should drop the C1 citation and remove its mention entirely.

action_items.item: Have a person keep investigating io-shop's errors. Start by asking checkout-platform for error data on io-pricing and io-summary-cache, and IO Payments Ltd for error data on io-pay, for the time around the alert.
Find and fix why io-shop's per-minute metrics returned nothing to the investigation around the alert.
Find and fix why io-shop's log lines returned nothing for the window before the alert.
Find out why the platform reported no pods for io-shop while its deployment showed replicas running, and fix the pod listing.
Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call rota so that it pages a person.
Make io-shop's deployment history record and name each revision it rolls out.

causal_chain.step: Requests to io-shop failed: the HighErrorRate alert reported io-shop's error rate above its threshold for {A1}. The metrics could not be read, so the alert is the only evidence of the failures, and how many requests failed was not measured.

The record does not show why the requests failed, and the evidence stops here. No minutes of metrics came back. No log lines came back for the window before the alert. The platform reported no pods, yet the deployment showed {T12.2} replicas running a revision the history does not name. No deploy, release or flag change came back for the day before the alert, and the flag provider showed no changes by anyone in the hour Argus read. Because none of these channels showed the service healthy, no change was tied to the incident and none was ruled out.

contributing_factors.factor: io-shop's telemetry came back empty to the investigation: no minutes of per-minute metrics and no log lines for the window before the alert. The platform also reported no pods while the deployment showed {T12.2} replicas.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: With metrics and logs to read, the investigation could have dated the onset and found what failed. A cause would then have been in hand instead of an escalation for insufficient evidence.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to an on-call incident, so nobody was paged.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been engaged when the alert fired. They could have started investigating and mitigating straight away, without waiting for Argus to escalate.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The deployment history does not name the revision the io-shop replicas run.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The running revision could have been dated and compared with earlier ones. That would have ruled a deploy in or out as the trigger.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well: Argus took the incident up {T2.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised and called in the Investigator straight away.
With every channel empty, Argus did not guess at a cause or act on one. It escalated for insufficient evidence {T17.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.

input.still_at_risk: Nobody found what raised io-shop's error rate, so it was still in place when Argus escalated and could still be failing requests.
